purpose: Restyle Docket's token-gated review page (/reviewer: the token form in web/login.html and the review app in web/src) into the Plain Standard look the front page already uses, and make every note on it say only what the document's record backs. Look only: behaviour, routes, API calls, token flow and actions are unchanged.
mechanism: web/login.html: the token form now uses the Plain Standard tokens and @font-face rules, in an inline style that carries the page nonce, and preloads the fonts from /home/fonts. docket/review_access.py: the reviewer CSP gains font-src 'self' so those fonts load. web/src/style.css: the review app restyled (queue, document sheet, candidates, picks, actions, a flat 'Nothing waiting' panel for an empty queue). web/src/main.ts: hasConflict() reads the conflict flag from the last 'shortlist' trace event and falls back to the hold reason 'conflicting_records' for older traces. When a conflict shows, a note under Candidates says every score is set to 0 because the clues name more than one unit outright, and each row reads 'Score 0, set by the conflict'. When another hold reason won, the outcome box adds the conflict line next to it. The outcome labels the raw value as 'Hold reason: <reason>'. Tier words: strong evidence, some evidence, and for tier none 'weak evidence, below the medium line'. A row whose own score is 0 with no conflict shows just 'Score 0'. The rules' pick note reads 'The rules list this unit first.', plus 'Compare the candidates with the document.' on a conflict. The suggestion note reads 'Suggested by the model. Nothing is filed unless you approve it.' Each pick card shows its note only when it has a unit. Tab order puts the rules' pick before the suggestion. DESIGN.md and .impeccable/design.json record the review page's look.
decisions: Plain Standard look reused from the front page, fonts served from /home/fonts (only font-src 'self' added to the CSP), over a separate look or font copy. The rules' note says 'listed first' rather than 'highest-scoring', because ties and zeroed scores (over the matching budget) make 'highest' false while 'first' is always true. Units named outright are not marked one by one, because conflict_record_ids does not reach the page; that is a follow-up, rejected here to keep the PR look-only with no backend fields. A zeroed row does not say why it is 0 (also a follow-up). The rules' pick comes before the model's suggestion in tab order (accepted product choice).
readers: DESIGN.md: whoever builds the next page in this look. README and docs/operations.md: people running Docket and reviewers (only if something they read about the review page is now wrong). Comments in web/src/main.ts, web/login.html and docket/review_access.py: the next maintainer of the review page.
